text:
About 2.2 lakh people in Hong Kong live in subdivided flats where the typical room is about 110 sq ft, smaller than a 135 sq ft parking space, at a rent of about ₹55,000 a month.

Why it matters: Hong Kong is not short of land. Only about 7% of it is residential and about 40% is protected country park, so the squeeze comes from how land is released, not from geography. Delhi is denser per sq km. Since March 2026 a new law sets a floor of about 86 sq ft with a window, and about 70% of these flats had registered by October.

Sources: HK Government (2025, 2026); AP (Feb 2025); Planning Department (2021).

Should cities set a minimum home size, even if it cuts the supply of cheap rooms?
